title: Denali Payments SOC 2 / ISO27001 evidence & RBAC/SSO scope review
summary: Redwood team walked through Trust Center access and control evidence flow for Denali's SOC 2 / ISO27001 review. Main items: RBAC and SSO integration plan, audit log retention/export, KMS key management options, and data residency controls. Action items include providing the SOC 2 report, Trust Center demo recording, and a proposed RBAC mapping spreadsheet. Agreed next step: trial access to Trust Center for Denali auditors and a technical deep-dive with Maya next week to validate log formats.
topics: RBAC / SSO mapping and SCIM sync
next_steps: Alex to share latest SOC 2 report PDF and Trust Center link (by 2026-03-05)
Priya to schedule technical deep-dive with Maya to review audit log schema and sample exports (by 2026-03-10)
Denali to provide list of internal auditors and required access windows for Trust Center (by 2026-03-08)
Set up short pilot environment with data residency region pinned to eu-west-1 for Denali test (target week of 2026-03-15)
action_items: Alex - share SOC2 report and Trust Center read-only demo link (due 2026-03-05)
Priya - export sample audit log schema + S3-compatible export example (due 2026-03-09)
Maya - provide list of required log fields and retention SLAs (due 2026-03-08)
Samir - confirm internal auditor contact details and NDA status (due 2026-03-07)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Denali Head of Compliance), Maya (Denali SecEng), Samir (Denali CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time. quick round robin? i can kick off with a 5 minute high level then priya will jump into the technical bits — sound good?
[00:18] Jordan: yep that works, we mainly want to validate evidence access and how auditors can pull reports from your trust center. also RBAC questions — who can see what.
[00:26] Priya: great, i'll try to cover the RBAC model, SSO / SCIM sync, and then go through logs and encryption. small caveat: some product names might be off in the transcript, sorry for any typos.
[00:40] Alex: quick context for Denali: you're on the payments stack, PCI-adjacent, preparing SOC 2 + ISO27001 assessments for Q2 correct?
[00:49] Samir: yes, timeline is end of Q2 for attestation. primary blockers are auditor access to evidence and making sure RBAC can map to our internal roles.
[00:58] Jordan: and data residency — our legal team wants eu residency for EU customers, so we need to ensure logs and any customer PII stay in eu-west region.
[01:10] Priya: understood. at a high level Redwood's Trust Center has two main pieces: downloadable compliance reports (SOC2/ISO cert PDFs and supporting artifacts index) and an evidence store that can expose canned exports for auditors — read-only links with expiry. we can set per-organization RBAC rules and also grant auditor roles.
[01:30] Maya: how is 'auditor role' different from 'admin'? we can't give full admin to auditors, obviously.
[01:36] Priya: auditor role is scoped read-only: you can view control mappings, download reports, and pull log exports. no config changes. it maps to a specific permission set in our RBAC layer. it can be disabled or time-limited.
[01:48] Alex: we also support time-bound SSO invites so you can provision via SAML or OIDC and set expiry windows, which is what folks usually do for auditor access.
[01:58] Jordan: SCIM? we use Azure AD SCIM profiles to auto-sync groups. can that integrate?
[02:05] Priya: yes SCIM provisioning supported. groups from Azure can be mapped to Redwood roles. note: group names sometimes get normalized, tiny mismatch occasionally — we've seen folks rename 'Auditers' -> 'Auditors' and the mapping breaks; small human errors.
[02:20] Samir: okay. for evidence, do we provide raw logs or preprocessed artifacts? our auditors want both sometimes.
[02:27] Priya: we can provide both. Trust Center exposes zipped evidence bundles (e.g., schematic control evidence, runbooks, screenshots) and we also offer raw audit log exports via S3-compatible endpoint or direct syslog push. exports include metadata for each event: timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, user_id (if tenant-level), and action.
[02:46] Maya: sample format? JSON lines? CSV?
[02:49] Priya: default is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson), but we can also export CSV for specific aggregations. the ndjson has the full event payload, with token-usage fields sometimes redacted if they include PII — there's a redact layer.
[03:02] Jordan: retention policy—what's default and can we extend? auditors want 12 months of immutable logs for now.
[03:10] Alex: hosted default is 180 days, but for Dedicated/Private customers we support custom retention policies and cold storage exports. for enterprise we can commit to 12 months via archive buckets and provide WORM-like retention semantics in the export.
[03:27] Samir: you'd provide the archive bucket in our AWS account or Redwood's?
[03:31] Priya: both options. for Private deployments we keep data in your VPC. for Dedicated you can choose to have the archive exported into your cloud account (preferred) or Redwood-managed bucket with strict controls.
[03:42] Maya: KMS — we need customer-managed keys. is HSM supported?
[03:46] Priya: yes. we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google CMEK) and you can bring-your-own-key. HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM are supported through the KMS provider. note that some ephemeral artifacts (cache keys) have separate lifecycles — we can provide key rotation windows and key-use logs.
[04:04] Jordan: audit logs for key usage — can auditors see KMS access logs?
[04:09] Priya: we surface KMS usage in the Trust Center as part of crypto controls. full low-level KMS API logs remain in your cloud account and we can include cross-referenced IDs in the exported evidence.
[04:22] Alex: i want to call out the controls mapping sheet — we have a template mapping Redwood controls to SOC2 criteria and ISO clauses. i'll share that spreadsheet after the call. it includes evidence pointers to specific log exports and config snapshots.
[04:37] Jordan: good, that's what we need. will reviewers need anything else?
[04:42] Priya: sometimes auditors ask for configuration snapshots (k8s manifests, terraform state) — we can export those as part of the evidence bundle if you're on Dedicated or Private and provide access. for hosted customers we provide exported config snapshots where possible but not infra-level secrets.
[04:59] Maya: question on RBAC: we have nested groups and delegated admins for payments ops, risk ops, and devs. can we implement role inheritance?
[05:08] Priya: Redwood RBAC supports role composition — you can create roles that include other roles. policies are attribute-based to an extent — resource-level scoping, organization-level, and route-level permissions. small caveat: nested roles can complicate audits; our mapping tool flattens the effective permissions which is helpful for reviewers.
[05:28] Samir: any known limitations around SSO providers? we use Okta and Azure AD both.
[05:33] Priya: both supported. Okta+SCIM and AzureAD+SCIM tested. older PingFederate setups sometimes need extra mapping.
[05:41] Jordan: data residency enforcement — how do you guarantee that data for EU customers stays in eu-west?
[05:47] Alex: we pin model serving and storage to region via tenancy configs. for Hosted we have multi-region hosting and tenancy tags that route traffic and store artifacts in the chosen region; for Private/Dedicated we deploy to your region. cross-region backups can be disabled.
[06:02] Maya: does that include logs and telemetry? some telemetry goes to telemetry.redwood.ai for product monitoring.
[06:09] Priya: telemetry that is product-internal is scrubbed of customer identifiers and aggregated; but for customers requiring strict residency, we offer an option to route telemetry to their own telemetry endpoint or to a regional telemetry collector. we'll note that in the SOW for Private deployments.
[06:24] Jordan: auditor access workflow — we want to give them read-only, but also limit the window and have an approval workflow. can we do that?
[06:31] Alex: yes: approve in console -> temporary role created -> SAML/OIDC session with expiry -> audit trail entry of who granted and when. we also support email + manager approval flows via our API for orgs that want extra gating.
[06:47] Maya: about logs, sometimes Redwood returns model debug artifacts that could include prompt text — how are prompts treated?
[06:55] Priya: by default prompts are considered part of the request payload. we have a configurable redaction policy: full, partial, or none. for compliance-sensitive customers we recommend partial redaction (hashing or truncation) and storing full prompts only in customer-managed encrypted archives.
transcript_continued:
[07:20] Samir: hash + truncate sounds good. any impact on model evaluation?
[07:25] Priya: partial redaction still allows token usage metrics and structural fields for evaluation without exposing full content. we can provide an evaluation pipeline that operates on pseudonymized data.
[07:36] Jordan: can we get a demo of the actual Trust Center UI for evidence retrieval? screenshots are fine for initial review.
[07:42] Alex: yes i'll share a recorded Trust Center walkthrough and a short live demo clip. link will be in the follow-up email.
[07:50] Maya: last technical question — log export schema: do you include KV cache events or only request/response traces?
[07:58] Priya: primary logs are request/response traces, routing decisions, and billing usage. KV cache hits/misses are included as summarized events not full cache content. we can include per-request cache metadata (hit/miss, key-id) in exports for performance audits.
[08:16] Jordan: would auditors accept those summarized cache events as evidence?
[08:20] Priya: usually yes, auditors want proof that caching was operating and not the actual cache contents. we include config versions and timestamps to correlate.
[08:30] Alex: ok let's talk timelines — Jordan you said you need to present to auditors next month?
[08:35] Jordan: preliminary audit window in late April, final in May. we need to provide access and evidence by mid-April so auditors can start sampling.
[08:44] Priya: we can target mid-April for evidence access. priority is SOC2 report and the RBAC mapping. i'll prepare the sample logs and a small S3 export for Maya to validate.
[08:55] Samir: any cost implications for extended retention and archival exports?
[08:59] Alex: yes additional storage and egress will be billed. we'll put together a storage estimate — generally archive pricing is discounted, but cross-account egress might incur standard cloud egress. we'll include a pricing note in follow-up.
[09:12] Jordan: legal also wants to know about subprocessor list and any third-party telemetry processors.
[09:18] Alex: we'll share the subprocessors list and our subprocessors' SOC2 reports link. for telemetry we can route to your processors for strict control.
[09:27] Maya: any caveat about dedicated vs hosted for compliance?
[09:31] Priya: Hosted is fine for many customers; Dedicated or Private is recommended for strict residency, BYOK, and deeper control. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and more control over snapshot exports; Private gives you full control in your network.
[09:48] Jordan: ok let's recap and next steps.
[09:51] Alex: recap: Alex will share SOC2 report + Trust Center clip; Priya will produce sample ndjson logs + S3 export example; Maya will send required log fields + auditor contacts; Samir to confirm region and NDA status. we'll schedule the technical deep-dive the week after next.
[10:10] Jordan: sounds good, thanks all.
[10:13] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up with links and the RBAC spreadsheet. bye.

Meeting end.
